1.1: independence comes naturally, so a year 1 can feel like home ground. The invitation is to begin something and also to let one other person in on it early.
1.2: listening is your first move, and a year 1 asks you to lead for once. Choose one thing you want and start it, even if nobody has asked you to.
1.3: expression is your strength, and a year 1 asks you to commit it to one direction. Pick the project you most want to be known for and begin it.
1.4: structure is where you start, and a year 1 asks you to begin before the plan is finished. Let a first version be rough and improve it as you go.
1.5: movement is your habit, so the fresh starts of a year 1 may come easily. The challenge is choosing one beginning and staying with it past the first thrill.
1.6: care is your instinct, and a year 1 asks you to start something for yourself. Put one hour a week into a project that serves nobody but you.
1.7: reflection is your home ground, and a year 1 asks you to act on what you have been thinking. Take one idea out of the notebook and make a first move.
1.8: effort is your engine, and a year 1 gives it a clean slate. Choose a goal that excites you, not only the one that is expected, and set it up to be sustainable.
1.9: the wide view is how you see, and a year 1 asks you to narrow it. After a long season of finishing, pick one new thing and give it your attention.
1.11: sensitivity is your signal, and a year 1 asks you to act on what you sense. Test one inspired idea in a small, concrete step instead of waiting for it to feel complete.
1.22: building is your method, and a year 1 invites a new foundation. Start small with the first stone, and resist planning the whole structure before you begin.
1.33: devotion is your nature, and a year 1 asks you to include yourself. Begin something that is for you and notice that it can still help others.

2.1: independence comes naturally, and a year 2 asks you to slow down and work alongside people. Let someone else's pace set the tempo for a while.
2.2: cooperation is your element, so a year 2 can feel like a deep breath. Use it to say what you want, since the quiet makes room for a real conversation.
2.3: expression is your strength, and a year 2 asks you to listen as much as you speak. Pay attention to what other people say beneath the jokes and the stories.
2.4: structure is where you start, and a year 2 asks you to let a plan bend to other people's needs. Ask what would make it work for the whole group, not only for you.
2.5: movement is your habit, and a year 2 asks you to stay put and be patient. The reward may be the kind of closeness that fast schedules rarely allow.
2.6: care is your instinct, and a year 2 deepens it through partnership. Let someone share the load and notice how it feels to be looked after.
2.7: reflection is your home ground, and a year 2 pulls you gently toward company. Share a half-formed thought with one trusted person and see what they add.
2.8: effort is your engine, and a year 2 asks you to ease off the throttle. Progress this year tends to come through agreements and relationships more than through force.
2.9: the wide view is how you see, and a year 2 brings it down to one or two people. Give someone close to you the attention you usually spread widely.
2.11: sensitivity is your signal, and a year 2 turns it up by a notch. Protect your rest, and check what you feel against what is actually being said.
2.22: building is your method, and a year 2 asks for patience with the people building beside you. A slower pace and a shared plan may produce a stronger structure.
2.33: devotion is your nature, and a year 2 asks you to receive as well as give. Let a partner or friend look after you in a small, practical way.

3.1: independence comes naturally, and a year 3 asks you to share what you start. Let your first projects be seen and enjoy the responses.
3.2: listening is your first move, and a year 3 invites you to be heard. Say the thing you usually keep back, with a little humor if that helps.
3.3: expression is your strength, so a year 3 can feel like turning up the volume. Choose a form, such as writing or music or talk, and give it a finish line.
3.4: structure is where you start, and a year 3 asks you to loosen it enough to play. Schedule time for something that has no purpose except enjoyment.
3.5: movement is your habit, and a year 3 gives it company and conversation. Invitations may multiply, so choose the ones that feed you.
3.6: care is your instinct, and a year 3 asks you to make it festive. Host something, celebrate a small occasion and let joy count as a form of care.
3.7: reflection is your home ground, and a year 3 asks you to bring it into the open. Write up, draw or talk through what you have been thinking, and share it.
3.8: effort is your engine, and a year 3 asks you to lighten up. Put some play into the work and notice that charm and enjoyment can help results.
3.9: the wide view is how you see, and a year 3 helps you put it into words. Tell the story of what you have learned, in a form others can enjoy.
3.11: sensitivity is your signal, and a year 3 gives it a voice. Express what you sense in art, words or conversation, and let it be imperfect.
3.22: building is your method, and a year 3 asks you to bring people in with enthusiasm. A good story about the project may do as much as a good plan.
3.33: devotion is your nature, and a year 3 asks you to enjoy yourself while you serve. Teaching and caring go better with a little laughter.

4.1: independence comes naturally, and a year 4 asks you to build something steady from it. Choose a few projects and give them regular, unexciting attention.
4.2: listening is your first move, and a year 4 asks you to turn it into dependable follow-through. Remember what people tell you and act on it.
4.3: expression is your strength, and a year 4 asks you to discipline it. A weekly writing or practice schedule may give your ideas somewhere to land.
4.4: structure is where you start, so a year 4 can feel like a natural fit. Take care not to let routine harden, and keep one evening a week unplanned.
4.5: movement is your habit, and a year 4 asks you to stay with one thing. Treat it as an experiment in what steadiness gives you that variety does not.
4.6: care is your instinct, and a year 4 gives it practical form. Fix the household system, plan the budget of your time and make the support you give sustainable.
4.7: reflection is your home ground, and a year 4 asks you to turn insight into method. Write down what you know and set it up as a routine or a plan.
4.8: effort is your engine, and a year 4 asks you to point it at foundations. Boring, careful work this year may make the next one easier.
4.9: the wide view is how you see, and a year 4 asks you to apply it to one concrete thing. Choose a task that benefits others and finish it properly.
4.11: sensitivity is your signal, and a year 4 asks you to build routines around it. Regular sleep, meals and quiet make a stronger base for intuition.
4.22: building is your method, so a year 4 may feel like a double dose. Keep the work in small, finishable pieces, and rest before you are tired.
4.33: devotion is your nature, and a year 4 asks for clear limits on it. Decide the hours and the tasks you can offer, and keep to them.

5.1: independence comes naturally, and a year 5 gives it room to roam. Try something unfamiliar on your own, then tell someone what you found.
5.2: listening is your first move, and a year 5 asks you to be more flexible about what you hear. Change may unsettle you, and your steadiness can help others adjust.
5.3: expression is your strength, and a year 5 gives it new audiences. Travel, meet new people and try a different form, but keep one project going to its end.
5.4: structure is where you start, and a year 5 asks you to bend it. Let a plan change when the facts change, and see what the flexibility teaches.
5.5: movement is your habit, so a year 5 may feel like a surge. Choose one anchor, such as a daily routine or a person, and let everything else vary around it.
5.6: care is your instinct, and a year 5 asks you to carry it into new places. You may find that home is portable and that others can look after the household for a while.
5.7: reflection is your home ground, and a year 5 pushes you out into the world. Test your ideas against real situations and people rather than only in thought.
5.8: effort is your engine, and a year 5 asks you to stay adaptable. Hold your goals loosely enough to change course when the situation does.
5.9: the wide view is how you see, and a year 5 gives it new material. Meet people unlike you, and let what you learn change a belief or two.
5.11: sensitivity is your signal, and a year 5 may feel like a lot of input. Choose stimulation on purpose and protect time to recover.
5.22: building is your method, and a year 5 asks you to hold the plan loosely. Expect revisions, and treat each as part of the design.
5.33: devotion is your nature, and a year 5 asks you to widen the circle. Take your teaching or care somewhere new, and allow yourself some time off.

6.1: independence comes naturally, and a year 6 asks you to check in with the people around you. Share a decision before it is made and notice what changes.
6.2: listening is your first move, and a year 6 gives it plenty to do. Home and family may need your attention, so keep some time that is only yours.
6.3: expression is your strength, and a year 6 asks you to turn it toward the people you love. Write the letter, host the dinner and tell the story that holds the family together.
6.4: structure is where you start, and a year 6 asks you to apply it at home. Organize the household systems so care feels light rather than heavy.
6.5: movement is your habit, and a year 6 asks you to stay close to home for a while. Commitments to people may bring a satisfaction that travel does not.
6.6: care is your instinct, so a year 6 can feel like a double measure. Watch the line between care and control, and ask before you help.
6.7: reflection is your home ground, and a year 6 draws you toward people. Let a household or a small group into your thinking, and let their questions shape it.
6.8: effort is your engine, and a year 6 asks you to spend it on the people who matter. Balance the work schedule with a standing time for family or friends.
6.9: the wide view is how you see, and a year 6 brings it home. Apply your sense of fairness to a specific relationship that needs attention.
6.11: sensitivity is your signal, and a year 6 gives it a lot of company. Home may be a place of rest or of overload, so set up a quiet corner for yourself.
6.22: building is your method, and a year 6 asks you to build something for the people near you. A home, a family tradition or a small community project may fit.
6.33: devotion is your nature, and a year 6 intensifies it. Say clearly what you can give, and let others hold their share.

7.1: independence comes naturally, and a year 7 suits it well. Take time for solitary study or work, and then share what you found with one other person.
7.2: listening is your first move, and a year 7 asks you to turn it inward. Spend time hearing your own preferences before the group's.
7.3: expression is your strength, and a year 7 asks for depth. Write, make or speak about something that matters to you, rather than something that merely entertains.
7.4: structure is where you start, and a year 7 asks you to examine it. Which of your routines and rules are worth keeping, and which are only habit?
7.5: movement is your habit, and a year 7 asks you to slow down. Try a retreat, a long walk or a quiet week and see what comes up.
7.6: care is your instinct, and a year 7 asks you to tend to yourself. Quiet time is not selfish, and it keeps your care honest.
7.7: reflection is your home ground, so a year 7 is a deep well. Keep a thread to other people, so that quiet does not slide into isolation.
7.8: effort is your engine, and a year 7 asks you to rest it. Use the slower months to think about what the work is for.
7.9: the wide view is how you see, and a year 7 helps you sort it. Decide which causes and relationships actually deserve your attention.
7.11: sensitivity is your signal, and a year 7 gives it room. Protect quiet, write down what you notice and give yourself time before you act.
7.22: building is your method, and a year 7 asks you to refine the blueprint. Study what has worked elsewhere, and test your plan before you commit.
7.33: devotion is your nature, and a year 7 asks you to look after your own depth. Take a pause from service and see what is left when you are not needed.

8.1: independence comes naturally, and a year 8 gives it something to push against. Take on a real challenge, and be generous with the people who help.
8.2: listening is your first move, and a year 8 asks you to speak up about what you want. Negotiating from a calm position can serve everyone.
8.3: expression is your strength, and a year 8 asks you to apply it to results. A clear message and a strong presence may open doors this year.
8.4: structure is where you start, and a year 8 gives it scale. Systems you have built may be asked to carry more, so check what needs strengthening.
8.5: movement is your habit, and a year 8 asks you to commit it to a goal. Direct your flexibility toward one ambition and give it sustained effort.
8.6: care is your instinct, and a year 8 asks you to take authority. Decide what is yours to lead, and let others do their parts.
8.7: reflection is your home ground, and a year 8 asks you to act on it. Turn your analysis into decisions and be willing to be judged by the outcome.
8.8: effort is your engine, so a year 8 may feel like full throttle. Put limits on your hours, and schedule rest as seriously as meetings.
8.9: the wide view is how you see, and a year 8 asks you to organize it. Take on a practical role in a cause you believe in, and be realistic about the resources.
8.11: sensitivity is your signal, and a year 8 asks you to hold it steady in a demanding setting. Plan for recovery after high-pressure stretches.
8.22: building is your method, and a year 8 may bring the chance to do it at size. Pace the effort and share authority with people you trust.
8.33: devotion is your nature, and a year 8 asks you to lead with it. Teaching, mentoring or managing can carry care into practical power, with firm limits.

9.1: independence comes naturally, and a year 9 asks you to finish what you started. Close out the projects of the past cycle before you start new ones.
9.2: listening is your first move, and a year 9 asks you to say goodbye well. Be honest and gentle in the conversations that end something.
9.3: expression is your strength, and a year 9 asks you to say what you have learned. A summing-up, a speech or a piece of writing may suit this year.
9.4: structure is where you start, and a year 9 asks you to clear space. Sort, archive and discard, and notice what the cleared space allows.
9.5: movement is your habit, and a year 9 asks you to complete a chapter before moving on. A farewell trip or a final decision may close the cycle.
9.6: care is your instinct, and a year 9 asks you to release what you carry for others. Hand back what is not yours, and forgive what has been holding you.
9.7: reflection is your home ground, and a year 9 helps you see the cycle whole. Write down what the last nine years taught you.
9.8: effort is your engine, and a year 9 asks you to tie off loose ends. Wrap up commitments, settle accounts of time and energy, and rest before the next cycle.
9.9: the wide view is how you see, so a year 9 can be intense. Be specific about what you are finishing, and let the rest wait.
9.11: sensitivity is your signal, and a year 9 may bring a flood of feeling about endings. Give yourself quiet and company in measured doses.
9.22: building is your method, and a year 9 asks you to finish a stage and hand it on. Document what you have built so that others can use it.
9.33: devotion is your nature, and a year 9 asks you to release those you have looked after. Trust that what you taught can stand on its own.
